messages:
oliver-cs: Heads-up — Customer PulseFin submitted their security questionnaire this morning and flagged two items: they need CAIQ answers + a downloadable audit-log export proving KMS-wrapped keys. They want evidence by EOD tomorrow (they keep moving the deadline). Also they report intermittent 401s when hitting /v1/audit/export. Can eng/security triage?
maya-cs: Thanks. Can someone confirm what exact export file they want (full audit stream vs filtered)? I asked for the form fields they expect.
sam-eng: I can look at the 401s — can you paste a sample request ID or request headers? 401 usually means expired/malformed JWT or missing audience.
oliver-cs: Customer sent a screenshot of error: "401 Unauthorized — invalid signature" and a service request id: rq_02b9f7a4. Also they attached the bespoke SIG form asking for KMS key origin + HSM attestations.
aj-security: For the SIG: we'll need to provide KMS policy docs, HSM vendor attestation (if used), and an explanation of key rotation cadence + audit log retention. For export proof we can produce a signed manifest showing objects were encrypted with the customer-specific key id.
ryan-sre: Looking at logs around rq_02b9f7a4 — see a short burst of 401s from their IP range at 2025-03-12T14:02:11Z. No deploys at that time. Rate limiting? Not obvious. Could be clock skew on their side causing JWT validation fails.
sam-eng: Agreed on JWT clock skew. Quick repro — can the customer run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/audit/export?start=2025-03-10&end=2025-03-11"
```
and paste the full response headers + request-id. If they get 401, get the token's `iat`/`exp` from their auth issuer.
maya-cs: I asked them for the curl output and for a list of specific CAIQ questions they need answered (they highlighted control items around CMK origin, HSM quotes, and retention exceptions). Also asked if they want a hashed export or full PII redaction.
aj-security: For HSM attestation — we can provide our HSM vendor's FIPS and attest report and a note that customer-controlled keys (BYOK) are supported in Private deployments. For hosted accounts we use KMS with envelope encryption; we can provide key lifecycle doc + rotation schedule.
ryan-sre: I pulled the audit logs export tool and generated a sample manifest (no customer data). Sam, can you help sign that manifest with the service key so we can show the customer the format? deploy-bot: export-job-started rq_02b9f7a4 (job id ej_8812).
sam-eng: I'll sign the manifest and attach a sanitized sample they can accept as evidence. Also will add a short note about JWT expiry troubleshooting.
maya-cs: Great — I'll tell PulseFin we have a timeline: sample signed manifest + CAIQ draft by EOD tomorrow, and troubleshooting steps for the 401 (curl + token iat/exp). Asking them for the curl output now.
oliver-cs: Thanks all. If they escalate further about a compliance audit window, escalate to enterprise ops (cc aj-security).
aj-security: One more: include the KMS key ARN and rotation policy snippet in the CAIQ responses. That usually satisfies most auditors.
ryan-sre: Noted. I'll keep monitoring for recurring 401s and correlate with rate-limit buckets.
maya-cs: PulseFin replied: "we got the curl output and token payload — token `iat` was 30s in the future from our server time" — they will sync clocks and retry. They also confirmed they want a redacted export + signed manifest.
oliver-cs: Perfect. Closing the loop here — keep me posted if the 401s continue after clock sync. Thanks team :thumbsup:
